name: Daily Dough
tagline: Invoicing app for UK freelancers and contractors: build an invoice, send it, chase it, see what got paid.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Invoicing for one person is mostly a form, a PDF template, and a paid/unpaid flag, and an agent will get you there in a session. What eats the weekend is everything around it: reliable email delivery so your invoice does not land in spam, sequential invoice numbering you never break, VAT handling if you are registered, and a template that looks like a business rather than a school project. Payment links mean a Stripe account and webhook handling, which is real work but not hard work. Where a DIY build genuinely hurts is at tax time, when your accountant wants exports and you want to trust the numbers. If you invoice a handful of clients on repeat, self-hosting is fine; if invoicing is how you get paid rent, the annoyance budget matters.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you store clients and line items, generate a numbered branded PDF invoice, email it, and mark it paid or overdue.
requirements: Node and a local Postgres or SQLite file
A transactional email provider API key, Postmark or Resend, in .env
Optional Stripe account if you want pay-by-link
Somewhere to run it if you want access away from your laptop
whatYouLose: Deliverability that has been tuned so invoices reach clients instead of spam folders
Polished invoice templates and a UI you do not have to keep fixing
Automatic payment reminders and chasing that actually fire on schedule
Accounting exports and MTD-adjacent tidiness your accountant will ask for
Mobile access and backups you did not have to think about
moatNotes: Nothing here is technically defensible. The defence is that an invoice is a document a stranger has to trust and pay, so ugly and unreliable costs real money.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because invoicing is a chore attached directly to income, and people will pay a small monthly fee to never wonder whether the email sent, whether the numbering skipped, or whether the PDF looked cheap. A self-built invoicer works right up to the evening you are tired, a client is chasing, and something silently broke. The paid product is buying the absence of that evening, plus a clean export when your accountant asks for one.
notes: Invoicing is the classic weekend build that quietly becomes a maintenance job the moment money depends on it.
prompt:
Build a single-user invoicing app for a freelancer. Local-first, no accounts, no signup, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, one file at ./data/app.db, with a small migration script.
- PDF generation with Playwright: render an HTML invoice template to PDF server-side.
- Email sending via the Resend API. Key in .env as RESEND_API_KEY. If the key is missing, log the email to stdout instead of failing.

Data model:
- settings: business name, address, email, optional logo path, VAT number, VAT rate, currency, payment terms in days, bank details text, next invoice number, invoice number prefix.
- clients: name, contact email, billing address, optional default hourly rate, notes.
- invoices: client, issue date, due date, status (draft, sent, paid, overdue), reference number, notes, and line items (description, quantity, unit price).
- payments: invoice, date, amount, method note.

Behaviour:
- Invoice numbers are assigned once, at the moment a draft is sent, taken from settings and incremented atomically. Never renumber, never reuse.
- Totals computed server-side: subtotal, VAT line if a VAT rate is set, total, amount paid, balance.
- Overdue is derived from due date plus unpaid balance, not a field a human sets.
- One clean, printable invoice template. Serif headings, generous whitespace, right-aligned totals block, bank details footer. It must look like a business sent it.
- Sending emails the client a short message with the PDF attached, and records sent_at.
- Dashboard: outstanding total, overdue total, paid this month, and a list sorted by oldest unpaid first.
- CSV export of all invoices and payments for an accountant.

Explicitly out of scope: multi-user, Stripe or any payment processing, expense tracking, time tracking, recurring invoices, quotes, multi-currency conversion, mobile apps.

Deliver: a seed script with one fake client and one paid invoice, a README with setup in five steps, and .env.example. Everything runnable with npm install then npm run dev.
